success_patterns: The clue was a paraphrase of a sentence in the passages. The agent matched on shared verbs and objects ('run out of ... mix lipstick with Vaseline ... cheeks') and read off the slot word whose type fit the category noun ('cheek cosmetic' -> blush). Several independent passages repeated this sentence.
The agent ignored a leading stage-direction parenthetical ('(Schumacher reads his clue.)'). It treated the director's name as an anchor and answered from the descriptive core of the clue.

For 'trapped in one of these' in a clue about a film, the agent found the passage on the film (Phone Booth, 2002, Colin Farrell). It saw that the film's title names the object the clue asks for, and gave that bare object term.

patch.reasoning: Both successes came from anchoring on the passage sentence or title that matches the clue's distinctive details, then giving the bare slot word. Rule 3 covers near-copies with a blank slot, but not paraphrased matches or the check that the slot type fits the category noun. Stage-direction parentheticals appeared in earlier rejected patches only bundled with other edits, so a small standalone rule is worth trying. The 'film title is the object' pattern is a reliable shortcut for 'one of these' clues about movies and books.

edits.target: A phrase repeated across independent passages is strong evidence.
edits.content: - The passage sentence is often a PARAPHRASE of the clue, not a copy. Match on the clue's verbs and objects ('run out of ... mix lipstick with petroleum jelly' ~ 'If you've run out of blush, mix a little lipstick with Vaseline and apply it to your cheeks'). Read off the word in the slot, then check that it fits the clue's category noun ('cheek cosmetic' -> 'blush'). Answer with that bare common noun.

edits.target: Jokes, asides and filler in the clue
edits.content: and leading stage-direction parentheticals ('(Schumacher reads his clue.)', '(Jimmy of the Clue Crew ...)')

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'Colin Farrell trapped in one of these' / 'the movie with X stuck in one of these': the clue describes a film or book whose own title often names the object ('Phone Booth'). Find the passage about that work (its title or first sentence repeats the actor, director and plot) and answer with the object term from the title, with no 'film' or year.
